title: Best ai trading platform that's been released so far?
author: Low-Paper-5010
selftext:
Over the past few months, I've seen a lot of mainstream brokerages/platforms release their own ai trading features on mainstream media outlets.Though I've also seen a lot of new upcoming platforms on social media being mentioned as well. 

So I was wondering what you believe is the best ai trading platform that's been released so far?

  
I'm down to try new ai trading platforms with new accounts just to see how it goes, but def would love to know if anyone else tried out the mainstream ai trading or the new upcoming apps.

comments.author: Baabic
comments.body:
Don't trust my Own Decisions at times.. not letting AI trade on my behalf 🤪
I use AI to score, unravel patterns, and recommend but not Trade...

For Institutional grade valuation, tracking markets, events, and tracking portfolios, and managing risks, etc.I like this
https://themarkets.ai/

It's free.

comments.author: Kozue_Sawada
comments.body:
I wouldn't trust any AI platforms to do the trades for me. I'm using AI for research, screening, doing the backtests or summarizing news, but when it comes to atual decisions and investing money, that part should still be human-approved. Too much could go wrong if u let a model jut" do its thing" without checking it. 
my thought is : use AI as a tool!

replies.author: Low-Paper-5010
replies.body:
Wait ya this is a great point and tysm for your response! What are your thoughts on using a hybrid model - where it uses ai gather signals from the news but then uses hard rules/deterministic code to make the trades? 

It’s mainly bc I’m trying to understand and navigate how ai can be used a tool and def agree it’s scary to use ai solely to make trades!

comments.author: mojovski
comments.body:
I use ai to build and run trading bots. 
Check out AI-Backbone.com 
If you want to build something sustainable and for long term, this is the way to go. Don't trust AI analyzing and predicting markets.

comments.author: ozgqr
comments.body: I’d compare these platforms by how reproducible their results are, not by the demo or headline performance: walk-forward tests, transaction costs, slippage, and a clear separation between research and live execution. That same audit trail would make it easier to evaluate whether Marx adds useful context without letting an AI make unchecked trades.

comments.author: yippe_noodless
comments.body: am trying to findd the best one for mee...

comments.author: dued62
comments.body: Before looking at specific platforms, you really need to look at the underlying architecture first. There is a massive structural gap between what the marketing implies on these new tools and what their actual code and legal footers say. Just do your due diligence first and ignore the marketing, hype, and FOMO. Stay away from these private waiting list deceptive marketing tactics.
